source_basename: Jack Lisowski vs Mark Selby - 2026 Quarter-Final.mp4
method: Continuous source-image sweeps followed by 10-25 fps contact inspection. Development windows informed fixes. Original frozen source labels are retained locally; subsequent timing and completeness corrections are explicitly recorded per window. This is not a full-match test set. Physical stops are not labelled.

windows.name: safety_exchange_holdout_5000
windows.annotation_note: Seven contacts were frozen and hashed before predictions were inspected. Review of an unmatched prediction revealed a real eighth contact at 5044.84-5044.88; the original review incorrectly grouped it with earlier referee repositioning. The original seven-contact reference and hash remain unchanged locally. All 300 overview samples were rechecked with predictions known. This corrected eight-contact interval is development data, not a complete blind holdout. The missed soft shot at 5017 subsequently informed detector changes. Bounds use decoded presentation times relative to video start, with native frame indexes recorded.

contacts.description: Soft head-on table shot. The white is stationary through the first frame; its lower edge advances in the next and continues forward with cue follow-through.
Live shot after earlier repositioning: player strikes the stationary white from the baulk rail; white travels down-table into reds.
Wide table shot. Cue reaches the white and the white launches away from the bridge in the next native frame.
Address close-up cuts to the wide table before contact. White launches from the baulk end at the cue tip, before the later cushion rebound.
Wide table shot with small white. First movement is subtle in the contact frame, followed by continuous travel and red collision; raw source pixels support the boundary.
Wide table shot. White starts moving at the forward cue stroke, followed by travel toward the reds.
Low oblique side view. White is stationary, then launches from the cue with blur and later black-ball motion.
Elevated close view. White launches at the cue tip, strikes a red, and then the broadcast returns to the main camera during the roll.
